events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet Friday, increasing to 7 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 6 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM Friday to 3 PM PST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. There is potential for moderate coastal flooding impacts at times, especially Saturday. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways.

events.title: Blizzard Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to 2 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph through Friday, then 60 mph Saturday into Sunday. * WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast. * WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard conditions will be intermittently possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...We are expecting a lull in snowfall beginning Friday afternoon through Saturday evening before snowfall chances increase Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the lull in snow and winds, expect higher visibilities. Winds will increase thereafter and be strongest on Saturday afternoon into Sunday with gusts as high as 60 mph possible, with blizzard conditions returning.

weather.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 13 at 6:07AM AKST until November 15 at 7:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph through Friday, then 60 mph
Saturday into Sunday.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...We are expecting a lull in snowfall beginning
Friday afternoon through Saturday evening before snowfall chances
increase Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the lull in snow
and winds, expect higher visibilities. Winds will increase
thereafter and be strongest on Saturday afternoon into Sunday with
gusts as high as 60 mph possible, with blizzard conditions
returning.
weather.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. A Blizzard Warning
means severe winter weather conditions are expected or occurring.
Falling and blowing snow with strong winds are likely. This could
lead to whiteout conditions, making travel extremely dangerous. If
you must travel, have a winter survival kit with you. If you get
stranded, stay in your vehicle.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet today, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet Friday, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers, Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM CST Friday the stage was 10.9 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Saturday evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early Sunday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:06PM CST until November 17 at 1:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CST Friday the stage was 10.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Saturday evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early Sunday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

events.description: * WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two inches. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph. * WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast. * WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard conditions will be intermittently possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The lull in snow and wind will continue through Saturday morning before snowfall chances increase Saturday afternoon through Sunday morning. Winds will increase thereafter and be strongest Saturday afternoon into Sunday with gusts as high as 60 mph possible and blizzard conditions returning.

location.region: Northern Arctic Coast

weather.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 14 at 4:05AM AKST until November 15 at 7:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The lull in snow and wind will continue
through Saturday morning before snowfall chances increase Saturday
afternoon through Sunday morning. Winds will increase thereafter
and be strongest Saturday afternoon into Sunday with gusts as high
as 60 mph possible and blizzard conditions returning.
weather.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. A Blizzard Warning
means severe winter weather conditions are expected or occurring.
Falling and blowing snow with strong winds are likely. This could
lead to whiteout conditions, making travel extremely dangerous. If
you must travel, have a winter survival kit with you. If you get
stranded, stay in your vehicle.

events.description: * WHAT...High risk of rip currents. events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 23 to 28 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 12:53AM PST until November 16 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf
Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up
to 23 to 28 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For
the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.
weather.areaDesc: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 25 to 30 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 11:58AM PST until November 16 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:

25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an
exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal
structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
weather.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,

surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep

Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

events.title: Marine Weather Statement
events.description: A moderate, long-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees will build across Hawaiian waters on Sunday and peak late Sunday and Monday as the period shortens to 13 seconds. The swell will produce moderate to heavy surges in north-facing harbors, especially at Kahului and Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these harbors should exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels and when entering or leaving port. The swell will diminish Tuesday.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers, Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM CST Saturday the stage was 13.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late this evening to a crest of 14.9 feet Sunday evening. It will then fall below flood stage Monday. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:02PM CST until November 17 at 12:24AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CST Saturday the stage was 13.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 14.9 feet Sunday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage Monday.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. River levels are expected to remain steady into next week. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water covers Mullet Lake Park. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 9.0 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 9.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 9.0 feet. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Seminole, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:51PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. River levels are
expected to remain steady into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on
Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water
covers Mullet Lake Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EST.
weather.areaDesc: Seminole, FL

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood Stage are forecast early next week due to a combination of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north through the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards inundated. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 6:30 PM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 2.6 feet. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Confidence is growing in the potential for a strong coastal storm to take a more northerly track through the Bering Sea mid-week. Depending on the final track of the system, minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts may be a possible for parts of the West Coast, with sea level rises between 3 to 7 ft possible. In addition to the coastal impact potential, periods of moderate to heavy snow and strong winds could begin as early as Tuesday night and last into Friday. The combination of winds and heavy snow could lead to reduced visibilities at times. We will continue to monitor this system closely and provide updates as additional information becomes available.

Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Mansfield TX from 20 to 60 NM... * Until 830 AM CST. * At 735 AM CST, a cluster of thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts was located 33 nm east of Malaquite Beach, or 39 nm southeast of Port Aransas, moving north at 180 knots. HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, with waterspouts possible. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and suddenly higher waves. * Locations impacted include... Port Lavaca, Port Oconnor, and Seadrift.

location.region: Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Mansfield TX from 20 to 60 NM

weather.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 15 at 7:37AM CST until November 15 at 8:30AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
SMWBRO

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Mansfield TX from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 830 AM CST.

* At 735 AM CST, a cluster of thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts was located 33 nm east of Malaquite Beach, or 39 nm
southeast of Port Aransas, moving north at 180 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, with waterspouts possible.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Port Lavaca, Port Oconnor, and Seadrift.
weather.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

events.description: A moderate, long-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees will build across Hawaiian waters and peak later today and Monday as the period shortens to 12 seconds. Mariners using these harbors should exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels and when entering or leaving port. The swell will diminish Tuesday.

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 15 at 5:07AM PST until November 16 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 22 to 25 feet with sets up to 28
feet possible.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From noon today to 4 AM PST Monday. .

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach
erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and Calhoun Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 AM CST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this evening through Monday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to anyone entering the surf.

location.region: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 15 at 4:15AM CST until November 16 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 AM CST Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, from this evening through
Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: At 500 AM EST, Satellite imagery is starting to indicate a potential for patchy dense freezing fog near the larger rivers and lakes. This could lead to slick spots on area roads, particularly bridges and overpasses along with railings, ramps, and elevated decks. Visibilities may be reduced to a quarter mile or less in fog. Use low beam headlights in areas of fog and slow down. Locations potentially impacted include... Somerset, London, Monticello, Williamsburg, Barbourville, Irvine, Mount Vernon, Beattyville, Manchester, McKee, Booneville, Whitley City, Boone, Fincastle, Science Hill, Burnside, Ravenna, Bunch, Bernstadt and Hightop.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 8 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this evening to 6 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this evening through late Monday night. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at 1115 PM tonight and again at 1122 PM Monday night.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 15 at 2:27AM CST until November 17 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
3 to 8 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip
Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this evening
to 6 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this
evening through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1115 PM tonight and again at 1122 PM Monday night.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 25 to 30 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 15 at 12:23AM PST until November 16 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 9:58PM PST until November 16 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain along the south slopes of the Olympics overnight will
push the Skokomish River above flood stage Sunday morning.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Saturday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tonight to a crest of 17.1 feet late Sunday morning. It will then
fall below flood stage early Monday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 630 AM PST.
